newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates edge up amid poor liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates edge up amid poor liquidity.

text.p: Croatian money market rates edged up slightly on Monday as demand sharpened amid poor liquidity of the banking sector, dealers said.
But the money and foreign exchange markets seemed unmoved by Franjo Tudjman's victory in Sunday polls that secured him another five-year mandate as Croatian president.
Usual money market creditors were short of kuna to lend after overall banking balances shrank to only 255 million kuna at the weekend.
Interbank call money loans accounted for most of the 42 million kuna settled by 0900 GMT. The rates were mixed at 10 and 10.5 percent, compared to an average 10 last Friday.
The central bank's Lombard lending also increased this morning to 30.6 million kuna from less than three at the end of last week.
"Liquidity is very bad, so some form of intervention with effect on Thursday or Friday will probably be needed," one bank official said.
Banks expected the central bank to call an auction to buy hard currency on Tuesday which would give them a new injection of kuna two days later.

The central bank said its foreign exchange purchases would intensify during the summer, when banks struggle hard to meet a seasonally stronger demand from tourists for the kuna cash. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
